query: tell me more about the Macklemore song
answer: Macklemore’s protest single “Hind’s Hall” was released on May 6 2024 as a single that supports pro‑Palestinian campus protests calling for an end to the Gaza genocide, divestment from Israel, and a ceasefire in the Gaza war [2]. The track is a protest song written, produced, and performed by Macklemore himself, and it samples “Ana La Habibi” by Lebanese singer Fairuz [2]. In its lyrics, Macklemore criticises the United States’ funding of Israel, describes Israel’s occupation of the Palestinian territories as apartheid, and condemns U.S. politicians who accept money from pro‑Israel lobbying groups such as Christians United for Israel (CUFI) and the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) [2]. The song was performed live during Macklemore’s Loop Tour shows at MetLife Stadium on September 4 and 5, where he also shouted “Free Palestine” and displayed images of Gaza’s devastation [4]. The performance of “Hind’s Hall” and Macklemore’s on‑stage statements led to his removal from the remainder of Ed Sheeran’s stadium tour [4].

sources.title: Macklemore Dropped From Ed Sheeran Tour After Onstage ‘Free Palestine’ Statements
sources.snippet: Macklemore — who’s been an outspoken supporter of Palestinians and those in Gaza for several years — joined the Loop Tour earlier this month, performing two shows at MetLife Stadium outside of New York City, on Sept. 4 and 5. At the first show, the Seattle rapper yelled “Free Palestine” onstage and expressed solidarity with people in Gaza and the occupied West Bank. He also showed images from the devastation in Gaza and performed his protest song, “Hind’s Hall,” about pro-Palestine [...] about pro-Palestine demonstrators at Columbia, who occupied a building and named it after Hind Raja, a six-year-old killed by the Israeli military. [...] Macklemore has been removed from the rest of Ed Sheeran’s stadium tour after several venues allegedly told the trek’s promoter that they would not allow the rapper to perform. The news came after Macklemore made several onstage statements in support of Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank and called for a “free Palestine.”
